title: Delay consumes a calculable distance
summary: Build the stopping envelope, then change one assumption.

steps.title: Declare the uncertainty
steps.caption: This example assumes a forward point mass, speed at most 1.1 m/s and position error at most 0.02 m. Braking authority is at least 2 m/s² after the delay.

steps.title: Motion continues during the delay
steps.caption: With τ = 0.20 s and forward acceleration at most 1 m/s², reaction travel is uτ + Aτ²/2 = 0.24 m. Speed can reach 1.3 m/s before braking begins.

steps.title: Brake from the later speed
steps.caption: Braking from 1.3 m/s requires 0.4225 m. Together with the earlier terms, required clearance is 0.6825 m. The 0.5 m wall lies inside this envelope.

steps.title: Change a bound, then validate it
steps.caption: With every other input fixed, reducing delay from 0.20 s to 0.18 s saves exactly 38.7 mm. That is model sensitivity, not a measured system improvement. A rejected admission does not stop the robot.
